title: Canonical constant-extension compact-coefficient comparison
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, $e\ge1$, a separated finite-type model $X_0/k_0$, the actual extension $D_e,X_{0,e}$ and fibre isomorphism $a:X_e\simeq X$ [def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data], and $\ell\ne p$, $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For a retained compactification $c$ of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport], let $c_e$ be its actual base change to $k_e$. The middle fibre map is the same canonical associativity isomorphism for the proper middle model. Form the section-normalized pullback square compositor [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category] on whole coefficient systems [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization]; take the proper right adjunction mate (with the identity-point unitor) and the inverse of the open left mate. Realize this composite on integral constructible objects by reduction, the actual system map, and total inverse limit, inserting the specified pullback counit [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and projection-normalized compact realizations on the two sides. A ConstantExtensionIntegralComparison retains the two square equations and proof of open-mate invertibility; its map is exactly this construction. Rationalize the map and apply the specified point fibre [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and coefficient embedding into $\Omega$ [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]. A ConstantExtensionCompactComparison is a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma_c(X,-)\simeq R\Gamma_c(X_e,a^*(-))$ of the recorded common-stage coefficient functors, normalized at every object's own finite representative to that explicit map, with equality endpoint transports. It contains neither a Weil operator nor a Frobenius equation. Given $R$ and a proof of ConstantExtensionRestrictionSpec [def-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-data], compose this fibre comparison with $R\Gamma_c(\alpha^{-1})$ for its retained carrier isomorphism and apply $H^r$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$. This defines the canonical comparison between the underlying modules of globalGeometricFrobeniusQbarCohomology [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] for $(D,X_0,F)$ and $(D_e,X_{0,e},RF)$.
